source: Exact follow-up method reported by independent agent next5_monitor; not a retained original controller file and not rerun for archive.
steps: Launch probe with subprocess.Popen, retaining that object; poll ready.json every0.01seconds with a5-second deadline.
Open pidfd using ready[pid], reported by this controlled child fixture. Controller/probe/child all originate by fork/exec in one namespace; no namespace switch or proc lookup.
Call process.send_signal(SIGINT) on owned probe Popen. Its second SIGTERM injection occurs after SIGINT was set to SIG_IGN but SIGTERM still had the raising handler.
Poll error.json; select the retained child pidfd, attempt actual TCP bind of the fixture address, and read case.command.json.
Assert pidfd not exited, listener not released, error signum SIGTERM, and no group_cleanup in command record.

After observing, cleanup via pidfd_send_signal(SIGKILL), await pidfd readiness up to3seconds, close descriptor, write parent-cleaned, then process.wait(timeout=5). Probe finally reaps its own directly owned children.
Persist observation.json and print the same object.
identity_description: The child pidfd was opened from controlled fixture ready PID, not literally controller Popen.pid. Probe retained its OwnedSession internally. No /proc inference.
counting: Independent reproduction of the same cleanup-transition defect; zero additional unique regression cases or kernel/VM results.
evidence_gap: Original controller existed only in a tool-inline Python block; exact executable source was not saved. Probe.py, observation, injection, source hash and raw command files remain unchanged.
